h: The Olah Makes Teshuvah Whole Through Self Surrender

p: is placed in the parsha next to the law of the olah,
while the olah is a single one
in the morning and in the evening.
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (זְבָחִים ז, ב)
(Mishlei 21:27) 'the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination';
one who transgressed a positive mitzvah and repented
for it does not come to atone for a positive mitzvah
"Never did a person spend the night in Yerushalayim
with a sin in his hand:
atoned for the sins of the night,
for sins committed during the day."
an olah does not atone at all,
to atone for a positive mitzvah
and for those liable for a positive mitzvah
is hard to explain of liabilities for a positive mitzvah,
אַךְ אִיתָא (בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ פָּרָשָׁה ז)
But it says (in Midrash Rabbah, this parsha, chapter 7, Vayikra Rabbah 7:3):
וְכֵן כָּתַב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ (כז, א)
and so wrote the holy Zohar, this parsha (III 27a):
"The olah: this is an evil thought," etc.
וּבָזֶה אִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קסד, ב)
And about this it says in the Gemara (Bava Basra 164b):
אֵין אָדָם נִיצּוֹל בְּכָל יוֹם כוּ׳
a person is not saved from every day," etc.:
(יְחֶזְקֵאל ד, יד) הִנֵּה נַפְשִׁי לֹא מְטוּמָּאָה
that I did not have thoughts by day
so as to come to impurity at night
what is so special about Yechezkel?
(דְּבָרִים כג, י) וְנִשְׁמַרְתָּ מִכֹּל דָּבָר רָע
(Devarim 23:10) "and you shall guard yourself from every evil thing,"
that one should not have such thoughts, etc.
because a person is not saved from this
is given in the Rambam (Hilchos Teshuvah 2:2):
that he will not return to sin again."
And at least it is necessary
that at that moment he be
in the state of having resolved
he was in the category of a penitent
(as we proved from the Gemara, Kiddushin 49b:
"on condition that I am a tzaddik").
וְכֵיוָן שֶׁאֵין אָדָם נִיצּוֹל בְּכָל יוֹם
And since a person is not saved every day
teshuvah is not conceivable for this,
he does not abandon it properly,
such that He could testify about him,
that he will not return to the sin again.
וְעַל זֶה בָּא כַּפָּרַת עוֹלַת הַתָּמִיד
And for this comes the atonement of the tamid olah;
and it rightly speaks of when there is teshuvah,
and it is not included in "the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination,"
the atonement of the tamid olah was needed,
for the teshuvah would not help,
since he is liable to return and sin;
For the meaning of the korban is
that he should picture to himself
he wants to offer his soul,
and he offers the animal in his place,
so that the blood of the korban be as his blood
and its fat as his fat.
in the prayer on a fast day:
a person would sin and bring a korban,
and only its fat and blood
may my fat and blood that have diminished be
as though I had offered them before You
And since at the time of offering the olah
that if he should again act
against the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
that he should offer an animal in place of his soul,
אֵין יֵצֶר הָרָע שׁוֹלֵט בּוֹ עוֹד
the yetzer hara no longer rules over him.
וּכְעֵין דְּאִיתָא בְּיִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And similar to what is said of Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him:
That is, Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
was commanded about the binding of Yitzchak,
because he was an established prophet,
כֵּיוָן שֶׁלֹּא אָמַר לוֹ אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
since Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, did not tell him
that he was commanded in prophecy to tell him
that he should consent to be an olah;
and it was possible that he could protest,
וְיִתְקַיֵּים נִסָּיוֹן אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and the test of Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, would be fulfilled
in his consenting in his heart
to offer him up as an olah;
and if Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
But Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
upon hearing that it was the will of Hashem Yisbarach,
wanted to do the will of his Creator
even though he was not commanded;
and this is what he said:
And although Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
to the fiery furnace in Ur Kasdim,
for a Ben Noach is not commanded
they wanted to make him transgress
and by the law of a Jew
one must be killed rather than transgress;
And although according to the Rambam, of blessed memory,
one who is exempt and gives himself up
וּבֶן נֹחַ אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְאַבֵּד עַצְמוֹ
and a Ben Noach may not destroy himself;
so stringent as to give himself up,
since he was still a Ben Noach
to give up the life of this world
and the life of the World to Come
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְקַדֵּשׁ שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל יָדוֹ
so that the Name of Heaven be sanctified through him.
(as they said, Midrash Rabbah, beginning of Toldos),
and his law is as a Jew,
and his mesiras nefesh was in accordance with the law.
מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Not so Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
who gave his life without obligation,
only out of fear of Hashem,
so as not to deviate from His will, may He be blessed;
he said, "I offered my soul before You,"
and from then the yetzer hara ceased from him,
כְּאִלּוּ הוּא צָבוּר עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
as though it were heaped on the altar;
He attached His Name to him in his lifetime,
that the yetzer hara would not lead him astray.
And this is what they said,
that the olah atones for thoughts of the heart,
which is like giving over his soul,
that he resolves in his heart
that to live against His will, may He be blessed,
שׁוּב אֵין הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שׁוֹלֵט בּוֹ
the yetzer hara no longer rules over him;
he is in the category of a complete ba'al teshuvah.
וְאַף שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ יִתְגַּבֵּר יִצְרוֹ עָלָיו
And although afterward his yetzer will overpower him,
for a person is not saved every day,
at the time of the deed
he was in the category of having done teshuvah,
so that He Who knows hidden things can testify about him,
on account of his broken heart,
אַף שֶׁאַחַר כָּךְ נִתְגַּבֵּר עָלָיו יִצְרוֹ
even if afterward his yetzer overpowered him
and he returned to his ways,
(as we proved from the Gemara in Kiddushin cited above).
And this is also what they said
that it atones for all Yisrael
and that too is with teshuvah,
only it would not have helped, as stated,
And this is why they said "with a sin in his hand,"
(and so it is hinted: (Tehillim 51:7) "Behold, in iniquity,"
on account of the serpent's counsel,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ מִדְרָשׁ תַּנְחוּמָא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת תַּזְרִיעַ
as they said in Midrash Tanchuma, beginning of Parshas Tazria,
according to the version of the Yalkut).
And this is why they used the phrase
"no person spent the night in Yerushalayim," etc.
which is from the shekalim of Yisrael
and even from outside the land
וְהָיָה לוֹ לְכַפֵּר עַל עֲוֹן יִשְׂרָאֵל
so it should have atoned for the sin of Yisrael
in all the places of their dwellings.
But according to what was said,
or in the rest of Eretz Yisrael,
where they did not know the exact
time of the offering of the tamid,
"as though he offered his soul" does not apply,
such that the teshuvah would help
where there were the anshei ma'amad
who stood by the offering of the tamid,
and each one resolved in his soul
that no person spent the night in Yerushalayim
with a sin in his hand,
through the offering of the tamid,
And Shabbos is a time of teshuvah,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (פִּרְקֵי דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פֶּרֶק יט)
דִּכְתִיב (תְּהִלִּים צב, ב) טוֹב לְהוֹדוֹת לַה׳
as it is written (Tehillim 92:2), "It is good to give thanks to Hashem":
that whoever confesses and abandons, etc.;
And this is what is said in the holy Zohar
and in Zohar Chadash, Ki Sisa 44b),
that Shabbos is in the secret of the bris,
to repair the blemish of the bris.
And this is what it says (Yeshayahu 56:2):
and keeps his hand from doing any evil":
for one who blemishes in this is called "evil,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א רִיט, ב)
as is written in the holy Zohar (I 219b)
one merits to repair the attribute of tzaddik,
And this is why there is placed in the parsha
terumas hadeshen next to the law of the olah:
as a remembrance of the dust of Yitzchak,
which is heaped on the altar;
that the yetzer hara ceased from him;
and likewise with the offering of the olah,
to atone for thoughts of the heart,
